speaker: richard_field
text: There. Thou asked for a chronicle. The second volume. Heavy as a hearthstone, and lent.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I will not sit yet. If it falls open, let it fall where it falls.

speaker: jacqueline_field
text: Set the near edge on the table, or it falls on your feet. I am not picking a hearthstone off the rushes.

speaker: richard_field
text: Thou art in the second Richard already. A king. His uncles. A cousin banished. A crown handed across. Thou found the reign without asking me for the page.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Four columns, then. I can read four on my feet.

speaker: richard_field
text: Read them. Four columns, and no play begun on my table. Thou wilt not make this room a tiring-house.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: A king, and more uncles than a scene would know what to do with. I am counting them. I am not writing them.

speaker: jacqueline_field
text: The stool is behind your knees. I have put it there. It can wait until a column asks for it.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: A cousin banished. I want the going of him, and I am still standing.

speaker: richard_field
text: Stand, then. Thou hast columns yet, and the gap on my shelf is already a fact. I can see the place it came from.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: A death in the margin of this, and I will not make the death a speech in thy room.

speaker: richard_field
text: It is lent. Lent in Lent, and I'll see the gap on that shelf every morning till it's home.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Thou wilt see the gap. I am not naming the morning I fill it.

speaker: jacqueline_field
text: Your knees have had enough standing to satisfy a sermon. The stool has had none of you. Sit if the next column is the last.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The last of the four. A landing, and the crown goes across. Lists, a banishment, a death, a landing, a crown handed across. No speech to go with any of them.

speaker: richard_field
text: Say the shape in thine own room. Thou art not beginning it here. The book is mine.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I am not beginning it. I am taking the shape away in my head, and the book in my arms.

speaker: jacqueline_field
text: These quires go where your feet are. The afternoon's work needs the place. You have the book.

speaker: richard_field
text: Thou hast heard her. The quires are the end of the visit. Take it in both arms.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Both arms. The gap is thine until it comes home, and the day of that is not today's business.

speaker: jacqueline_field
text: The door is wide enough if you turn sideways. I have moved paper. I have not scolded you off the step.

speaker: richard_field
text: Go, then. And thou, bring it back a book, not a playhouse. I will know the difference by the gap.

speaker: jacqueline_field
text: Do not stop on the landing for a fifth column. Four is what I put the stool out for.

speaker: richard_field
text: Four columns, thou. A fifth in the doorway would be a play, and the doorway is not having one.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Four. I can count to four without beginning a fifth. A book. Both arms. No speech in it yet.
